Charter 0.1.0 is the first public release of the OAuth 2.1 authorization server for WordPress, built to work especially well with MCP while remaining useful for other protected WordPress REST integrations.

## Highlights

- Turn a WordPress site into a site-local OAuth 2.1 authorization server with standard authorization-server and protected-resource discovery.
- Connect public desktop, command-line, hosted, and MCP clients through Authorization Code with mandatory PKCE S256.
- Issue short-lived, resource-bound access tokens and optional rotating refresh tokens with replay containment and revocation.
- Keep WordPress roles, capabilities, object permissions, REST permission callbacks, cookie authentication, nonces, and Application Passwords authoritative.
- Let users review consent, inspect connected applications, and revoke complete grants from their WordPress profile.
- Give administrators client and grant governance, issuance pause, Bearer lockdown, security health, retention, and signing-key controls.
- Support isolated per-site issuers on Multisite under required network activation.

## Security

Charter applies exact redirect and resource matching, bounded OAuth abuse controls, protected Client ID Metadata Document retrieval, explicit client provenance on consent, single-use authorization codes, rotating refresh tokens, and secret-free operational logging.

## Requirements

- WordPress 6.9 or later; tested through WordPress 7.1.
- PHP 8.4 or later.
- HTTPS for public sites. Explicit local development may use HTTP.
- Multisite installations must network-activate Charter and enable each site issuer separately.

Charter is an OAuth authorization server. It does not provide MCP tools itself, replace WordPress authorization, or act as an OpenID Connect provider.
